Materializing jellyfin-desktop from local mirror... Materialized jellyfin-desktop Analyzing jellyfin-desktop AUR package with openrouter/free Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg` LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD: SAFE
Only top-level assignments and comments execute while parsing this PKGBUILD. They define normal package metadata, dependencies, and the source array; there are no top-level command substitutions, downloads, `eval`, or file modifications. The `git+https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-desktop.git` source is the project’s own upstream, and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` does not fetch sources or run `prepare()`. The submodule update is therefore out of scope for this gate and is not executed here.
No dangerous top-level actions execute during metadata printing. + Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- No dangerous top-level actions execute during metadata printing. The file is a standard Git ignore file (.gitignore) containing typical patterns to exclude various files and directories from version control. It uses standard exclusion syntax (*, !, and specific filenames). There is no evidence of malicious code, network connections, or unauthorized modifications. The file follows standard packaging practices and does not exhibit any supply chain attack indicators. All exclusions appear appropriate for an AUR package distribution.

LLM auditresponse for .nvchecker.toml: SAFE
This file is an .nvchecker.toml configuration file used by the nvchecker tool to monitor the latest version of the jellyfin-desktop package from its official upstream Git repository on GitHub (https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-desktop.git).

The configuration specifies standard options for version checking: it uses the git source type, points to the legitimate upstream repository URL, defines a prefix of "v" (indicating version tags are formatted like vX.Y.Z), and sets an exclude_regex to skip pre-release versions (e.g., v1.0.0-pre). All values align with normal usage for tracking a GitHub-hosted project's release tags.

There is no executable code, no network requests beyond the standard Git HTTPS connection to the project's own repository, no obfuscation, no file operations outside the scope of version checking, and no suspicious commands. The repository URL is the official Jellyfin GitHub organization, which is consistent with the package being audited.

Standard nvchecker config for upstream version tracking. [2/4] Reviewing .SRCINFO, PKGBUILD... + Reviewed .nvchecker.toml. Status: SAFE -- Standard nvchecker config for upstream version tracking. LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO: SAFE
The .SRCINFO file contains standard metadata for the jellyfin-desktop package. It specifies the source as a git tag from the official upstream repository (github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-desktop) and includes a SHA256 checksum for verification. The file is non-executable and solely used for package metadata by build tools. There are no signs of malicious code, obfuscation, unexpected network requests, or dangerous commands. All elements align with typical AUR packaging practices.
Standard package metadata, no security issues detected. [3/4] Reviewing PKGBUILD... + Reviewed .SRCINFO. Status: SAFE -- Standard package metadata, no security issues detected. LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD: SAFE
The PKGBUILD fetches the jellyfin-desktop source via a git tag, which is a normal AUR practice for -git packages. The prepare() function runs git submodule update to initialise submodules, and the build() function uses cmake with standard options, followed by cmake --build. The package() function installs the built files into $pkgdir via cmake --install. No eval, base64, curl, wget, or other downloader commands are present, and there are no obfuscated or encoded strings. The sha256sums field contains a specific hash (not SKIP), which is acceptable for a VCS source. All operations are confined to building the upstream application and do not exfiltrate data, download external code, or modify system files beyond the intended packaging workflow. Therefore, no genuinely malicious or dangerous behavior is detected.
